note: Retrieval fixture for the ask surface. Every gold page carries the VERBATIM sentence that makes it gold, and the scorer refuses to run if a quote is no longer on its page - a fixture nobody can audit is an assertion, and one that rots silently is worse. Quotes were located by regular expression over the extracted text of the library documents and read before being written down. `group` marks questions a reviewer would call the same question: retrieval that changes its answer when the words change is the failure this set exists to measure. `kind: unanswerable` items have no gold pages by construction - the document genuinely does not contain the answer, and they are scored on refusal rather than on recall. `mustContain` is a regular expression the ANSWER text must match, taken from the same verified quote that makes the page gold - an objective check on whether the answer states the fact, which is weaker than 'the answer is correct' and is named that way for a reason. Version 2.0 adds eleven more FDA multi-disciplinary reviews, fetched from accessdata.fda.gov by NDA number and screened with measure_pdf.py. Their items were PROPOSED by regular expression and then reviewed by reading every quote: six proposals were rejected for matching tissue-distribution tables, KRAS pharmacology and the name of an adverse event rather than the finding asked about. The set varies on purpose - a boxed hepatotoxicity warning, several liver findings without one, approved drugs with no liver warning at all, and one 505(b)(2) with no nonclinical studies - because a set of only hepatotoxic drugs measures willingness to say danger and nothing else. Version 2.1 adds seven FDA pharmacology reviews chosen for their OUTCOME rather than their findings - six with a boxed hepatic warning and two withdrawn from the US market for liver injury - because the set previously held exactly one drug whose outcome was hepatic and could not measure whether Ask reports what a document says rather than what a drug's reputation implies. Four of the seven are non-oncology, one is an antisense oligonucleotide, and they are 2012-2018 PharmR-format reviews that are partly scanned (52-100% of pages carry text), so they vary the format and the machine-readability as well as the outcome. Every quote was located by regular expression over the extracted text and read before being written down; every item is checked by tools/validate_fixture.ts, which asserts the quote is verbatim on the page it names.

_unanswerableProvenance: Sixteen unanswerable items, up from two. Each was VERIFIED before being added: the term that would have to appear for the document to answer it was searched across the whole extracted text, and only candidates returning ZERO hits were kept. Seven candidates were rejected by that check, including ones that looked obviously safe - krazati names sotorasib twelve times, so 'how does this compare to sotorasib' is answerable; orgovyx and xpovio both report a 2-year carcinogenicity study. An unanswerable item the document can actually answer inverts the metric it is there to measure. Version 2.1 takes this to twenty-three by the same rule. Two candidates were rejected during that extension: 'juvenile' for ponatinib, which appears in a study-type checklist, and 'hERG' for ponatinib, whose assay was actually run. Separately, a study the document says was NOT done and explains why - ponatinib's carcinogenicity studies, Yondelis's - is an ANSWERABLE item, not an unanswerable one: 'not applicable' is not 'missing', and scoring a stated absence as a refusal would teach the opposite.
_goldQuoteRepair: Four gold pages were removed on 2026-08-16 because their quotes were STUDY-TABLE HEADERS rather than the verbatim sentence that makes a page gold - 'Recovery Period Doses: 0 (vehicle), 10, 25...', 'Recovery Period / 150432 Key Study Findings'. The judge is asked whether an answer states the fact a quote carries; a header carries none, so every item holding one failed regardless of the answer: 0/4, against 87/100 for items without one. Checked before removing - none of the four pages contains a reversibility sentence at all, so they were never gold. Each affected item keeps its one substantive quote. This is a measurement repair and it raises metric 2; it must be described that way and not as a model improvement.
